item: The baseline-tag backfill reads the three columns it matches on, in id-ordered chunks of 20,000, instead of every keyword as an entity at once
summary: backfill_baseline_tags loaded the whole keyword table as ORM entities in one pass (an operator action with no bound). Measured on 1,500,000 seeded keywords, same store, statement before and after: 33.8 s and 2,951 MB of Python allocation (3,272 MB resident growth) against 3.7 s and 12.5 MB as the three columns the match reads (id, language, normalized_term) in id-ordered chunks. A chunk is 20,000 rows of the widest shape the columns allow (10-character language, 255-character term), which peaks at 11.8-12.0 MB (about 600 B a row) whatever the table holds on the read side (the new KeywordTag rows stay pending until the one commit, autoflush being off, so memory still grows with the tags added); no clock decides where a chunk ends. LIMIT: the cursor is the id, so a keyword inserted with an explicit id BELOW it between two chunks (a merge import; the app's own inserts take the next autoincrement id) is not seen until the next run, which is idempotent. tests/test_baseline_backfill_chunks.py (14 tests; the statement test fails on main).
